shortDescription: Makes pure anvil repairs (repair material or unenchanted sacrifice item) cost no XP levels
oneLiner: Repairing a damaged tool, weapon or piece of armour in an anvil - with its material or by combining it with an unenchanted second copy - costs zero XP levels, works even on gear vanilla calls "Too Expensive!", restores 50% more durability per material unit by default, and accepts extra materials such as diamonds for netherite gear, prismarine shards for a trident or sticks for a bow.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: With JEI installed, FreeAnvilRepairJeiPlugin registers one anvil recipe per extra_repair_materials entry whose item AND material resolve and whose item is damageable (fully damaged item + material -> item repaired by a hardcoded 25%), so players can look the extra combos up in JEI's anvil tab. Nothing is lost without JEI: the class is loaded solely by JEI's own annotation scan (compileOnly API + localRuntime, no dependency in neoforge.mods.toml), and the repairs work regardless. The JEI entries also disappear when the module is disabled or free_material_repair is false, and the displayed 25% ignores repair_boost_percent (see notes 8).

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Four default extra_repair_materials entries target Create's diving gear (create:netherite_diving_helmet/boots with diamonds, create:copper_diving_helmet/boots with copper ingots). Without Create those ids do not resolve and the entries are skipped silently (debug log only) - nothing breaks, there is no compile-time dependency in this module. Per CHANGELOG.md:970 the diving gear would already be repairable free through the regular vanilla material path; the entries are explicit insurance.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: NOT an integration - there is no code link to Quark in this module at all (no ModList.isLoaded, no compile dependency, no toml entry). It is a documented override: Quark's own diamond repair patches the vanilla anvil code path and charges XP, and since this module answers AnvilUpdateEvent first and computes the result itself, Quark's version never runs for those combos, so the repair stays free. The default extra_repair_materials list is described in-source as 'Quark-style' (same item=material idea).

mixins: free_anvil_repair.AnvilMenuFreeRepairMixin (BOTH sides - listed in the "mixins" block of vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json:21, not in "client", and as the standalone jar's only mixin in build.gradle:433-434; targets net.minecraft.world.inventory.AnvilMenu with a single cancellable @Inject at HEAD of mayPickup(Player, boolean) that sets the return value to true when the result slot is filled, getCost() == 0 and FreeAnvilRepairModule.allowFreePickup() - i.e. for ANY cost-0 output, not only this module's)
events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AnvilUpdateEvent (FreeAnvilRepairModule.onAnvilUpdate, @SubscribeEvent; the module instance is registered on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize, FreeAnvilRepairModule.java:63-67)
recipes: No crafting/datapack recipes and no loot hooks. What it does inject are anvil repair COMBINATIONS from extra_repair_materials (defaults: all 9 netherite tools/armour pieces + diamond, Create's 4 diving-gear pieces + diamond/copper ingot, trident + prismarine shard, bow + stick), handled purely in code via AnvilUpdateEvent and mirrored into JEI's anvil tab by FreeAnvilRepairJeiPlugin when JEI is present. These extra combinations only exist while free_material_repair is true.

configKeys.effect: Repairing with the item's repair material (e.g. diamonds) costs no XP levels. Also the master switch for extra_repair_materials: with false, those non-vanilla combinations stop working altogether instead of just costing XP.

Combining two items of the same type costs no XP levels, as long as the sacrifice item is damageable and carries neither enchantments nor stored enchantments (pure durability merge). The kept item may be enchanted.

Whether free repairs still double the hidden prior-work penalty (REPAIR_COST component via AnvilMenu.calculateIncreasedRepairCost) like vanilla does; default false so repairing does not make later enchant operations more expensive.

Extra durability restored per material unit on every module-handled MATERIAL repair, vanilla material and extra_repair_materials alike: perUnit = max(1, maxDamage/4 * (100+value)/100). 0 = vanilla 25%/unit; the default 50 = 37.5%/unit, so 3 units fully repair an item instead of 4. Does NOT apply to combining two of the same item, and the JEI display ignores it.

Additional anvil repair materials (Quark-style, format item=material, one item may appear in several entries). These repairs are computed by this module and are free like regular material repairs (and follow repair_boost_percent). Entries whose item or material is not installed are skipped silently; the config validator additionally rejects entries with no '=', with '=' at either end, or with a second '='.

notes:
CORRECTION (2026-09-20, commit 25325d4) - THIS SUPERSEDES ANY STATEMENT BELOW ABOUT PACKAGING.
`waystone_amethyst_repair` IS now in build.gradle's `standaloneModules` list, so the free-repair coupling is no longer bundle-only. Run standalone, the sibling module detects this one through `ModList.isLoaded("vpa_free_anvil_repair")` - jar presence, not its `enabled` flag.
Everything further down that calls the module bundle-only, says it has no standalone jar, or reports a grep over build.gradle returning nothing was written before that commit and is out of date. The rest of the research below is unaffected.

SOURCE FOOTPRINT (everything this module owns, verified by find + grep): modules/free_anvil_repair/FreeAnvilRepairModule.java (263 lines), modules/free_anvil_repair/config/FreeAnvilRepairConfig.java, modules/free_anvil_repair/compat/jei/FreeAnvilRepairJeiPlugin.java, mixin/free_anvil_repair/AnvilMenuFreeRepairMixin.java, standalone/free_anvil_repair/FreeAnvilRepairStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_free_anvil_repair") -> StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot). A grep for DeferredRegister / KeyMapping / Dist. / Minecraft.getInstance / registerCommand / ModList / shouldInitialize / isEnabledByDefault / @EventBusSubscriber / LootTableLoadEvent / AddReloadListener over all five files returns ZERO hits: no registries, no items, no blocks, no entities, no commands, no keybinds, no mod gate, no enabled-by-default override (Module.java:73 default true applies). No lang keys either - grepping "anvil" in en_us.json only hits command.vpa.bmsigns.icon.anvil, which belongs to bluemap_signs.

1) HOW IT WORKS (module javadoc, lines 23-42). The module does NOT patch anvil cost. It listens to AnvilUpdateEvent, recognises a "pure repair", recomputes the repair result itself and calls event.setOutput(result) + event.setCost(0). Every other anvil operation is left untouched -> vanilla costs. Because a non-empty output on the event replaces vanilla's own createResult computation (NeoForge's AnvilUpdateEvent contract - the NeoForge source is not in this repo), gear whose prior-work penalty already showed "Too Expensive!" is repairable again. The repaired stack is left.copy(), so enchantments, custom name and every other data component survive untouched.

2) WHY THE MIXIN EXISTS. Vanilla AnvilMenu.mayPickup requires cost > 0, so a cost-0 result could not be taken out. AnvilMenuFreeRepairMixin (@Inject at HEAD, cancellable) returns true when the result slot is filled (the boolean parameter is ItemCombinerMenu's result-slot hasItem()), self.getCost() == 0 and FreeAnvilRepairModule.allowFreePickup(). SURPRISING SIDE EFFECT: it does not check WHO produced the result - it makes ANY non-empty cost-0 anvil output takeable, including one set by a third-party AnvilUpdateEvent handler. The only justification in the code (mixin javadoc, lines 11-17) is that vanilla itself never produces a non-empty cost-0 result.

3) DELIBERATE CROSS-MODULE COUPLING. modules/waystone_amethyst_repair/WaystoneAmethystRepairModule.java:29-32 + :40 + :112 asks ModuleManager whether "free_anvil_repair" is enabled and sets cost 0 in that case, riding on exactly this mixin for the pickup - so the Warp Stone repair is free only while THIS module is enabled. waystone_amethyst_repair is NOT in build.gradle's standaloneModules list (grep "waystone" build.gradle -> no hit), so that coupling exists only inside the bundle jar. cat_guardian/item/CatArmorItem.java:70 and axolotl_guardian/item/AxolotlArmorItem.java:62 likewise document that their scute repairs become free through this module (their repairs work by themselves; only the 0-level price comes from here).

4) THE THREE EXCLUSION RULES, all in onAnvilUpdate (lines 86-108). (a) left must be non-empty, isDamageableItem() and getDamageValue() > 0; (b) right must be non-empty; (c) isRenaming aborts everything (lines 115-123: a typed name that differs from left.getHoverName(), or a blank name on an item that HAS a CUSTOM_NAME, i.e. clearing it; a null name is not a rename). Renaming WHILE repairing therefore keeps full vanilla cost. The sacrifice path additionally requires the SACRIFICE to be the same item, damageable, and free of both enchantments and STORED_ENCHANTMENTS (isPlainSacrifice, lines 170-175) - the left/kept item may be enchanted. Sacrifice repair also bails out when there is no improvement (newDamage >= left damage, line 233) and leaves that case to vanilla.

5) repair_boost_percent (default 50) IS A REAL GAMEPLAY CHANGE THAT README DOES NOT MENTION. repairPerUnit = max(1, (maxDamage / 4) * (100 + boost) / 100), so by default every MATERIAL repair (vanilla material AND extra_repair_materials) restores 37.5% of max durability per unit -> 3 units fully repair an item instead of 4. Explicitly NOT applied to the sacrifice/combine path (comment at lines 229-230). Sacrifice math stays plain vanilla: leftRemaining + rightRemaining + 12% of max, and applySacrificeRepair sets no material cost, so the whole right stack is consumed.

6) GOTCHA - extra_repair_materials DEPENDS ON free_material_repair. Both the vanilla-material branch and the extra-materials branch sit inside the same `if (getConfig().isFreeMaterialRepairValue())` (lines 100-103). Setting free_material_repair = false does not merely restore XP costs for the extra combos: those combinations are unknown to vanilla, so they stop working ENTIRELY (netherite + diamond, trident + prismarine shard, bow + stick all become invalid anvil inputs again). Only the vanilla-known material repairs fall back to paid vanilla behaviour.

7) TWO DEFAULT ENTRIES ARE NEW ANVIL BEHAVIOUR, not "a free version of a vanilla repair": minecraft:trident=minecraft:prismarine_shard and minecraft:bow=minecraft:stick. Vanilla has no repair material for either item.

8) JEI DISPLAY IS NOT THE REAL REPAIR AMOUNT. FreeAnvilRepairJeiPlugin.registerRecipes builds the "after" stack as maxDamage * 3 / 4 with the comment "one material unit restores ~25%" (line 86) - it hardcodes the VANILLA 25% and ignores repair_boost_percent, so with the default boost the shown recipe understates the real repair (37.5%). It also skips entries whose item is not damageable (maxDamage <= 0, lines 77-80) in addition to unresolved ids, and registers nothing at all when the module is disabled or free_material_repair is false (lines 44-54).

9) QUARK INTERACTION (javadoc of isExtraRepairMaterial, lines 125-131, plus CHANGELOG.md:970). Because the module answers AnvilUpdateEvent first and computes the result itself, mods that patch the vanilla anvil code path - the comment names Quark's diamond repair - never run and cannot charge XP for the same combination. There is NO code link to Quark in this module: no ModList.isLoaded("quark"), no compile dependency, and the bundle's neoforge.mods.toml declares no quark (and no jei) dependency at all - only create, at lines 83-87.

10) CONFIG VALIDATOR vs. RUNTIME PARSER MISMATCH. The defineList validator (FreeAnvilRepairConfig.java:85-91) additionally rejects any entry containing a SECOND '=' (s.indexOf('=', eq + 1) < 0), while the runtime parser (parseExtraRepairMaterials, lines 142-164) only splits on the first '=' and would happily accept it. Such an entry is therefore corrected away by NeoForge's config spec before the parser ever sees it (what exactly NeoForge does with a rejected entry - drop it or reset the list - is not visible in this repo). Malformed entries that do reach the parser are logged with warn("Ignoring malformed extra_repair_materials entry ..."); entries whose item or material id simply is not installed are skipped silently (debug log only, and only when debug_logging is on).

11) DEAD BRANCH: applyMaterialRepair's `if (damagePerUnit <= 0) return;` (lines 199-201) can never trigger - onAnvilUpdate already guarantees getDamageValue() > 0 and repairPerUnit() returns at least 1, so min(damage, perUnit) >= 1.
